So a name does not always have two parts. docker rm: "Remove one or more containers". stage-1 compose api: build dockerfile DonHang.Api/Dockerfile, image donhang-api:stage-1 - verified.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: In a name such as `caddy:2.10.0`, the part before the colon is the image's name and the part after it is the tag, a label that usually marks one version of that image.

issues.text: Overgeneral syntax. Docs give the name as [HOST[:PORT_NUMBER]/]PATH[:TAG]; the tag is optional (default `latest`) and a registry port adds another colon. "has two parts" is true for every name in this lesson but not as a rule.
issues.quote: An image name has two parts: before the colon, the name; after it, the tag, a label for one version of that image.
issues.fix: Replace with the suggested_text of claim 9: "In a name such as `caddy:2.10.0`, the part before the colon is the image's name and the part after it is the tag, a label that usually marks one version of that image."

issues.text: Ambiguous agent. The lesson uses "the lab box" for the `donhang-lab` container; "built by the lab" can be read as built inside that container. It is built by Compose (`scripts/up.sh` runs `docker compose up --build`) from `DonHang.Api/Dockerfile` on your machine.
issues.quote: the API's image, built by the lab from its own `Dockerfile`
issues.fix: Replace with: "the API's image, which `scripts/up.sh` builds from `DonHang.Api/Dockerfile`".

issues.text: The closing question confused me. Right after "two different running servers", "which of the two" reads as "which of the two Caddy servers is the lab box", and the answer (section 5) is neither: it is `donhang-lab`. I had to guess that "the two" meant image vs container.
issues.quote: How can one thing be the source of two different running servers, and which of the two is the lab box you have been SSH-ing into?
issues.fix: Replace the second half with: "and is the lab box you have been SSH-ing into an image or a container?"

issues.text: Image tag is never explained. The text writes images as `name:something` (`caddy:2.10.0`, `donhang-lab:stage-0`, `...:version-10.3_p1-r1`) and Try it expects "(tag `stage-0`)" in `docker images` output, but nothing says the part after the colon is a tag, i.e. a version label for the image. Not in known_vocab.
issues.fix: Add one sentence in section 5 after the FROM explanation: the part after the colon in an image name is its tag, a label naming one version of that image.

issues.text: "pinned" is jargon I do not know. I can guess "base image" from the FROM sentence, but not what makes it pinned or why that matters for identical output.
issues.quote: on the same pinned base image
issues.fix: Replace "pinned base image" with "base image, named with an exact version in `FROM`" (or say in one clause what pinned means).
